title: unified-quant-artifact-format-and-canary-metrics
creator: Amina Patel
description: Standardize a single artifact and manifest format for quantization profiles (INT8 / FP8 / GPTQ / AWQ) and implement a canary + regression detection pipeline that validates perf and quality before publishing profiles to the model catalog. This ticket defines the v1 artifact schema, CI verification hooks, canary telemetry, gating thresholds, and automated rollback rules that the serving runtime and Console will consume.
acceptance_criteria: Artifact format v1.0 manifest schema published and adopted by quant pipeline (fields enumerated below)
CI job that validates artifact signature, checksum, and runs a standard micro-benchmark suite on a pinned hardware target (GPU type) is green
Canary pipeline produces time-series metrics (latency/throughput/quality) for each candidate profile; regression detector flags regressions per policy
Automatic catalog publish blocked if regression detector flags high-impact issue; manual override requires documented review and audit entry
Console shows per-profile performance summary and a link to the canary run artifacts and diff report
manifest_schema_summary: model_sha256: hex string pointing to base model binary used for quantization
quant_type: one of [INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ]
quant_bits: numeric (e.g., 8 or 4); empty for FP8 where not applicable
calibration_dataset_hash: hash pointing to the calibration corpus used
op_kernel_signature: list of kernels/optimizations required (for runtime kernel selection)
expected_microbenchmarks: object-level string mapping to sample p50/p95 latency and throughput for canonical sequence lengths
profile_semver: x.y.z for the quant profile itself
manifest_signature: PGP-signed blob or KMS-signed token
compatibility_matrix: list of compatible runtime versions and hardware families
implementation_plan: Design manifest v1.0 and publish spec with examples (this doc)
Extend quant CI to emit manifest alongside artifacts and sign via CI KMS key
Add lightweight micro-benchmark harness that runs using a pinned Docker image on a single hardware SKU and uploads metrics to the canary bucket
Implement regression detector lambda that ingests canary metrics, compares to baseline profile in catalog, and emits a pass/fail + confidence score
Hook canary detector into catalog publish pipeline: on fail -> block publish + create incident + notify owners; on pass -> promote to staged catalog
Console: add profile page with metrics, artifact link, and 'pin-to-model' action
Docs: update onboarding README and developer guide with schema and publishing flow
telemetry_requirements: Latency: p50, p95, p99 measured for sequence lengths [16, 128, 1024] and batch sizes [1,4,8]
Throughput: tokens/sec for same canonical shapes
Memory: GPU memory peak and stable working set (MB)
Quality: evaluation harness scores (answer-similarity, incr-LL, instruction-following pass rate) for the canonical eval set

Regression signals: relative change vs baseline for p95 latency (> +15% triggers warning), throughput (>-10% drop triggers warning), quality (>+1.5% relative degradation in primary metric triggers fail)
Telemetry labels: quant_type, quant_profile_semver, runtime_version, gpu_family, benchmark_hash, ci_run_id
canary_playbook: 1) Upload artifact + manifest to canary bucket via CI (signed)
2) CI triggers canary-run job on pinned cluster (single dedicated node matching target sku)
3) Run microbenchmarks and quality evals; collect metrics and artifacts (logs, perf traces, diff files)
4) Regression lambda compares metrics to baseline profile (catalog entry) and emits verdict with confidence and top-3 contributing metrics
5) If verdict == fail and confidence > 0.8 -> block publish, create issue in Linear with links, tag owner, and schedule postmortem
6) If verdict == warning -> notify owners for manual review; allow publish with explicit override and audit note
7) On pass -> automatically stage profile in catalog under 'staged' and seed Console preview page
constraints_and_tradeoffs: Single artifact schema simplifies consumption but may omit per-hardware micro-optimizations (we will include op_kernel_signature to surface these)
Micro-benchmark on a single SKU reduces CI cost but may miss regressions on other hardware families; mitigation: sampling matrix for heavyweight profiles
Strict regression thresholds prevent regressions at the cost of potentially higher false positives; initial threshold tuned conservatively to reduce user impact
Signed manifests introduce KMS management overhead but are required for traceability and secure pinning in Private deployments
